answer: Ivory-marked continuity ledger. Each identity must publish a signed state chain whose newest block references a fresh random challenge seeded from a public beacon, like a gale-driven weather feed. Duplicate agents diverge at the fork, and any peer can submit the two conflicting heads as proof. The yarrow test is deterministic: the ledger accepts only the longest chain with no equivocation, so clones either stay silent (losing work) or expose themselves. Cost: one full re-registration plus forfeiture of all accrued chain history per clone, making N copies cost N times the compute and storage.
